samples.summary: Requiring a non-empty `file` makes a blocking finding that cites no file impossible to rebut locally — and refuses the whole run
samples.evidence: `unusableRebuttalReason` (spec-to-pr.mjs:633) rejects any record whose `file` is empty, and `readRebuttalRecords` (spec-to-pr.mjs:713-718) turns that into a hard throw that aborts the run. But `file` is NOT a required finding field: review-panel.mjs:91-122 lists `required: ["severity","confidence","summary","claimType"]` only, `carryForwardFindings` (prior-findings.mjs:166-179) carries such findings forward with `file` simply absent, and `renderBlockingFindings` (spec-to-pr.mjs:338) prints them as "(no file cited)". Matching such a finding is possible: `findingSimilarity` (rounds.mjs:522) compares `trimmed(a.file) !== trimmed(b.file)` and `trimmed = String(s ?? "").trim()` (rounds.mjs:480), so a file-less rebuttal matches a file-less finding exactly. The result is that a repo-level blocking finding (no `file`) can never be disputed through `--rebuttals`: the record is refused, the command exits 1 before the panel runs, and since an un-rebutted finding is re-raised every round (spec-to-pr.mjs:1206-1208), the loop cannot converge past it. The intended rule is 'a rebuttal that can match nothing is refused'; the implemented rule is stricter than that in exactly the case the finding itself omitted a file.

samples.summary: Re-keying `reviewBase` on the checkout silently orphans every existing round store: in-flight branches restart at round 1, losing carry-forward and resetting the round bound
samples.evidence: `reviewBase(branch, repo)` now hashes `${repo}\n${branch}` (spec-to-pr.mjs:839-842) where previously it hashed only the branch, and nothing migrates or even notices the old directory. For any branch already mid-loop, the next `spec-to-pr.mjs review` resolves a different base, so `roundsOnDisk(base)` (used at spec-to-pr.mjs:1061) returns [], `nextRound` yields 1, `priorFindingsFor` (spec-to-pr.mjs:1146) carries nothing, and `roundBoundNotice(spentRound)` sees zero spent rounds. That is precisely the pair of failures the file goes to great lengths to prevent elsewhere: reviewing without the carry-forward (the stated reason `prepareRoundInputs` exists) and slipping past the non-convergence bound the `--fresh` handling at spec-to-pr.mjs:1071-1087 refuses to let anyone do silently. The user gets no signal — the run prints 'self-review round 1' as if it were a fresh branch.

samples.summary: `unusableRebuttalReason` coerces non-string `lens`/`file` with `String()`, so structurally junk records pass the new guard and adjudicate nothing silently
samples.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:630/633 test `String(r.lens ?? "").trim()...` and `String(r.file ?? "").trim()`. A record such as `{ lens: {}, file: 7 }` yields "[object Object]" and "7", both non-empty, so the guard passes and `normalizeRebuttals` (line 665) writes `lens: "[object Object]"`. `adjudicateRebuttals` partitions with `(typeof r?.lens === "string" ? r.lens : "") === lensId` (review-panel.mjs:2328-2330), so that record reaches no lens — the exact silent-loss failure the guard was added to eliminate — while still being counted in the 'adjudicating N rebuttal(s)' line (spec-to-pr.mjs:1153). A `typeof === "string"` requirement (as `parseRebuttalComment`'s stricter contract implies) would close it.

samples.summary: A `--rebuttals` file whose JSON is not an array is reported as 'holds no usable records', not as the wrong shape
samples.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:710 coerces a non-array parse result to `[]` for the unusable scan, and `normalizeRebuttals` does the same at line 663, so a hand-written file containing a single object `{ lens, file, claim }` (a very natural mistake) falls through to `--rebuttals file holds no usable records` at line 720. That message tells the author their records were rejected rather than that the top-level value must be an array, which is the one thing they need to fix. Related nit on the same throw: `record #${i}` at line 716 is 0-based, so the second record is reported as '#1'.

samples.summary: A non-string lens id in panel.json makes the newly exported `blockingFindingsIn` throw an uncaught TypeError after the panel has already run
samples.evidence: The filter at spec-to-pr.mjs:1199 keeps any entry with `p.conclusion !== "success"` without checking `typeof p.id === "string"`, and `blockingFindingsIn` (line 957) calls `path.join(outDir, lens, "verdict.json")` — `path.join` throws `TypeError: Path must be a string` for a numeric/object id, and that throw is outside the function's try (it happens while building the argument list only for `readFileSync`; the join itself is inside the try, but the earlier `blocking.map((p) => p.id)` is not sanitized, so the same id is also interpolated into the summary line at 1202). The result is a stack trace in place of the blocking report the command exists to print. Low probability since panel.json is produced by our own panel, but the blocking report path has no other guard.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `unusableRebuttalReason` rejects any record whose `file` trims to empty (spec-to-pr.mjs:633-635), and `readRebuttalRecords` escalates that to a throw (spec-to-pr.mjs:713-718) which `cmdReview` turns into a hard `fail()` before the panel runs (spec-to-pr.mjs:1148-1152). But `file` is NOT required of findings: the panel schema requires only severity/confidence/summary/claimType (review-panel.mjs:122) with `file` a plain optional property (review-panel.mjs:96); `carryForwardFindings` preserves its absence via `dropUndefined` (prior-findings.mjs:147-151,166-169); and both the local report (spec-to-pr.mjs:338 "(no file cited)") and the adjudicator prompt (review-panel.mjs:2207 "(no file given)") explicitly render file-less findings. The stated justification — that a file-less rebuttal can match nothing — is false in this case: `findingSimilarity` gates with `trimmed(a.file) !== trimmed(b.file)` where `trimmed = String(s ?? "").trim()` (rounds.mjs:480,521-522), so two absent files compare equal and scoring proceeds; the panel applies no further file filter, partitioning only by lens (review-panel.mjs:2329) after an object-only load (review-panel.mjs:2662-2665). Hence a repo-level blocking finding with no `file` cannot be rebutted locally, and the attempt aborts the entire run (dry-run included) instead of being adjudicated; the cloud channel has the same restriction (rebuttal.mjs:203-205), so there is no bypass. No guard makes this unreachable and it is a wrong-condition/logic defect in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The code at spec-to-pr.mjs:839-843 is as quoted (hash over `${repo}\n${branch}`, single call site at :993, no migration), but the finding's harm requires pre-existing round stores written under an older branch-only key. The trusted baseline (main, checked out to .trusted per .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:530-537) contains no persistent round store at all: .trusted/scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:282 creates a throwaway `mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir(), "spec-to-pr-review-")` directory per run, and reviewBase/roundsOnDisk/branchKey/nextRound/priorFindingsFor/roundBoundNotice do not exist in that file. The keyed store, carry-forward and round bound all arrive together in this change, so no shipped code ever wrote a branch-only-keyed `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review/...` directory — there is nothing to orphan, no carry-forward to lose, and no prior spent rounds for the bound to miss. The only residual case is an author who ran an intermediate commit of this same unmerged branch locally: a one-time, non-destructive, self-healing re-key of a /tmp scratch directory for a local dev convenience script (CI runners get a fresh tmpdir per job, so rounds never persist across runs there). Not blocking.
